subject: Streaming fragment loss causing throughput degradation — urgent escalation to execs
messages:
From: Jake Reynolds <jake@fintegrate.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jan 2027 17:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production: fragmented streaming + throughput collapse (region us-west)

Rishi / Redwood team,

We started seeing a spike in broken streaming responses in our production service starting ~16:45 PST. Clients report partial payloads where the WebSocket/HTTP chunked response stops midway and the client reconnects. Overall QPS for our streaming routes has dropped ~38% and we are seeing an uptick in 502/504 during chunk reassembly.

Attached is a short capture from our edge showing repeated FIN/RECV sequences and a few server-side 502s. Repro steps (intermittent):
- Open WebSocket to /v1/realtime; send prompt A (long, multi-turn).
- After ~12-20s output is delivered in 2-3 fragments, then stream stops and the connection stays open but no more chunks.

This is impacting latency SLAs and blocking a live demo tomorrow. Can someone confirm whether this is on Redwood runtime or our network?

Thanks,
Jake Reynolds
Head of Platform
Fintegrate

Attachment: capture-20270129-ws-log-snippet.txt
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jake Reynolds <jake@fintegrate.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jan 2027 17:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: fragmented streaming + throughput collapse (region us-west)

Jake — thanks for the report and the packet/snippet. We're investigating immediately. Initial questions:
- Is the behavior only on the realtime streaming endpoint or also on bulk chunked generation?
- Any correlation with specific model versions or message sizes?

I've looped in Monica (infra) and Connor (SRE) to triage. Monica/Connor — can you pull the gw/runtime logs for Fintegrate's tenant (tenant_id FIN-009) around 16:30-17:30 PST and confirm whether we saw outbound chunk flush failures or SIGPIPEs on the worker pool? Also please preserve the affected worker IDs for postmortem.

I'll keep you posted every 30m; if we confirm a regression we'll escalate to platform leads and execs.

—Rishi
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, Jake Reynolds <jake@fintegrate.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jan 2027 08:09:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec flag: streaming fragment loss affecting Fintegrate — request for immediate allocation

Laura / Vivek — elevating for executive visibility. Fintegrate (strategic account; deal in evaluation, contract pending) is experiencing streaming fragment loss that has reduced their throughput ~38% and is causing demo instability. Impact: potential churn in due-course PoC and escalations to their CTO if not mitigated before Monday.

Summary of what we know so far:
- Symptom: WebSocket and chunked-transfer responses stopping mid-stream while connections remain open; clients reconnect and sometimes get 502.
- Time window: 2027-01-29 16:45–17:30 PST.
- Affected routes: /v1/realtime primarily, with a small number of /v1/generate chunked requests.
- Customer reported QPS drop ~38% and elevated error rate.
- Internal signals: transient socket write failures on worker pool; increased backpressure metrics on router; a small fraction of workers showing kernel-level ECONNRESET traces.

Immediate asks:
1) Exec approval to preemptively shift a portion (~20%) of Fintegrate traffic to a dedicated fallback pool (different worker binary with conservative kernel settings) and enable prefix-caching bypass to see if symptom reduces. This will increase cost but reduces customer impact.
2) Approve a hotfix rollout for improved chunk-flush timeouts (infra change) and temporarily cap max-concurrent-streams per worker.
3) Communication approval: I propose we send a short status update to Fintegrate and their execs acknowledging impact and ETA for mitigation.

Attached: quick capture and an initial graph of pipeline QPS. Relevant links: INF-9876, runbook on drive.

Requesting your go/no-go and any additional direction — we have Monica and Connor ready to execute mitigations.

—Rishi
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 30 Jan 2027 08:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Exec flag: streaming fragment loss affecting Fintegrate — request for immediate allocation

All — brief update and mitigation plan from infra/SRE: 
- Root suspicion: interleaved kernel TCP buffer pressure combined with aggressive async write coalescing on the worker binary; results in occasional dropped write completions and apparent "stalled" chunk writes.
- Immediate mitigations implemented (08:30 PST):
  * Enabled conservative write-flush timer (was 200ms, set to 800ms) on the affected pool
  * Shifted 22% of Fintegrate traffic to the fallback pool (worker version v1.4.2-fallback) with slower batching but more predictable IO behavior
  * Temporarily capped max-concurrent-streams per worker from 48 -> 24 for Fintegrate tenant routes
- Observed effect (08:55 PST): chunked-drop events down by ~75%, QPS trending back up (~+21% since mitigation), and error rate normalized toward baseline.

Next steps:
- Prepare a hotfix rollout with a conservative write backoff for the mainline binary (INF-9876).
- Collect full worker core dumps for 3 affected hosts and attach to the Jira ticket.
- Draft customer-facing status note (Rishi) — recommended language below.

Attachment: pipeline-qps-20270130.png; fallback-routing-config.diff

—Monica
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jake Reynolds <jake@fintegrate.com>, Asha Patel <asha@fintegrate.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 31 Jan 2027 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Update: mitigation in place + next steps / postmortem scheduling

Jake / Asha — quick update following infra mitigations:
- What we changed: routed ~22% of your streaming traffic to a fallback worker pool and adjusted write-flush timers and concurrency caps.
- Immediate result: we observed a ~75% reduction in chunk-drop events and a partial recovery in throughput (+21% from low). Error rates have dropped toward normal.

We understand the timing is poor relative to your demo; our remediation is intended to stabilize your production traffic and buy time while we validate the mainline hotfix. Next steps:
- We will run a staged hotfix rollout (INF-9876) over the next 48 hours with monitoring hooks; if stable we'll revert the fallback routing.
- We propose a joint postmortem on 2027-02-02 at 10:00 PT to review root causes and long-term fixes.

Appreciate your patience — we will share the postmortem artifacts and worker dumps post-retrospective. Please let us know if you'd like a short call before the demo.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
